{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1991 | image = | dates = 19 May – 1 September 1991 | teams = 16 | connacht = | munster = Tipperary | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = Antrim | matches = 16 | poty = [[File: Colours of Tipperary.svg|border|20px]] [[Pat Fox]] | team = Tipperary | titles = 24th | captain = [[Declan Carr]] | manager = [[Michael Keating (hurler)|Michael 'Babs' Keating]] | team2 = Kilkenny | captain2 = [[Liam Fennelly]] | manager2 = [[Ollie Walsh]] | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = [[File: Colours of Tipperary.svg|border|20px]] [[Michael Cleary (hurler)|Michael Cleary]] (3–35) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1990|1990]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1992|1992]] }} The '''1991 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 105th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 19 May 1991 and ended on 1 September 1991. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]] but were defeated by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the Munster final replay.{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/was-final-the-best-game-of-hurling-ever-to-be-played-30571635.html|title=Was final the best game of hurling ever to be played?|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=23 May 2016|date=9 September 2014|first=Colm|last=Keys}} [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] qualified for the All-Ireland quarter-final as winners of the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship|B championship]]. On 1 September 1991, Tipperary won the championship following a 1–16 to 0–15 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final. This was their 24th All-Ireland title, their second in three championship seasons. Tipperary's [[Michael Cleary (hurler)|Michael Cleary]] was the championship's top scorer with 3–35. Tipperary's [[Pat Fox]] was the choice for [[Texaco Hurler of the Year]]. == Team changes == === To Championship === Promoted from the [[All-Ireland Senior B Hurling Championship]] * Derry * Westmeath
